sections.name: PersonaPage
sections.title: Analyst profile content
sections.what: Checks the analyst name is valid, or shows not found. Shows the name and chip, a card with sport, skill domain, signature tool, and skill words, and a section for the signature tool. That section has a status label, plus links, a table, or a receipt, depending on the tool's kind. If the analyst has example wording, it appears at the bottom.
sections.why: Likely reason: the status label tells users how far to trust each tool's data.
sections.watch_out: Illustrative tables show example numbers with no receipt, so a user who misses the status label could take them as real.

summary: Profile page for one AI analyst, showing its card, its signature tool, and its example wording of the facts.
purpose: Presents one analyst and what it does.
why: Users browse the analysts, and the status label explains how solid each tool's data is.
how: Steps in order: the page checks the analyst name is valid, and shows not found if not. It looks up the analyst, its tool, and its voice. It shows the card, then the tool section with content chosen by the tool's kind, then the example wording if one exists. It also sets the tab title.
inputs: The analyst name in the web address, the analyst list, and the roster service results.
outputs: A profile page, or a not-found page.
risks: Illustrative tables show example numbers with no receipt. Every analyst shares the same tab title. A pending tool shows only a note.
debug: If a tool section is blank, check the tool's kind and its rows. If an analyst is not found, check the analyst list. If the example wording is missing, check the roster service's voice list.
